title: Harborlight Camp
intro: Teal enamel mug beside the folded map, compass toward the pane
Beyond the harbor, the ridge still held a thin stripe of morning mist
Papa Bear checks weather, trail notice, return time before we pack
I check torch, water, notebook, spare layer — we each carry the route
verse1: I set the teal mug on the map so the breeze can't lift the sheet
Cream compass to the pane; the ridge still holds a stripe of mist
Papa Bear — field guide, rust-colored coat, patience that earned the name
Weather, trail notice, return time checked before he loads the pack
Torch, water, notebook, spare layer — I check; we each carry the route
If weather changes we turn back. That's the plan, not a debate
We leave the table clear and carry out everything we brought
A good look starts with careful arrival and time to notice
At the trail I photograph the board and match it to the print
Wooden marker to the sheltered ridge; no shortcut changes the plan
Harborlight Camp on a fresh page, my finger tracing the path
Overlook: he shows how the same landmark shifts from a new angle
Footbridge short from the shore, long from above — I draw both views
I label where I stood. I don't declare that one sketch is wrong
Brighter hillside doesn't pull us off the marked route we named
We keep to the path and walk on toward the marked campsite
chorus1: Harborlight, keep the mug on the map
Don't rush the sky. Don't force the fact
Describe the view you can actually see
Leave room on the page for uncertainty
verse2: Tent on designated level ground. We keep the walking path clear
Telescope stays in the case while we check the tripod feet
Mug on the low table, away from the edge
Clip on the notebook so the pages can't blow free
Thin cloud crosses the first evening star. I wanted the whole sky
Papa Bear says record the cloud as part of the view, don't pass it by
First entry: pale sky, one bright point, breeze coming off the water
The page is useful already — it names what we can actually see
Lantern down, shield toward the table, a small circle of warm light
Enough to find mug and notebook; beyond it, ridge and sky show clearer
He keeps the telescope off the sun's last glow and waits for full dark
Turns at the eyepiece. I describe a bright point. I don't guess how far
He asks what changed: cloud moved, harbor lights sharper, pale band faded
A brief streak while both of us look up — no time to draw the whole path
Direction, approximate time, the fact it lasted a moment
The notebook leaves room instead of forcing a name on the light
chorus2: Harborlight, keep the mug on the map
Don't rush the sky. Don't force the fact
Describe the view you can actually see
A glimpse stays a glimpse — not a grand discovery
verse3: For a while we say nothing. The quiet is shared attention
Hands around the mug. Last line: waiting gave a view rushing would miss
Before bed we compare notebook and route plan, line by line
Place, weather, time, observer named. Sketches labeled as sketches
An uncertain identification stays uncertain on the page
That way the notes work for someone who wasn't beside the telescope
Morning I count the table: mug, notebook, clip, lantern, telescope case
Papa Bear checks the site for scraps and loose equipment
We leave it as clear as we found it and take the same marked path
Overlook: the footbridge looks different again in morning light
I add a third small drawing. The first two still sit in sight
Nothing in the old sketches needed to be erased
Together they show how position and light can change an honest look
Back at the open window, teal mug beside the folded map
Four pages of notes, three small sketches, the mug back in its place
Describe the evidence before you decide what it means
bridge: I had hoped to see everything at once.
Record the cloud as part of the view, he said.
The streak crossed. Neither of us drew its entire path.
We wrote direction, time, a moment. We left the rest open.
Morning light didn't cancel the shore. It added a third drawing.
chorus3: Harborlight, mug home beside the map
Three views of the bridge, and nothing erased
Describe the evidence before deciding what it means
The record is enough. We don't need a more dramatic story
